title: Why Apple just killed the iPhone

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: If Apple "killed" the iPhone, what future would replace it—and why might that be necessary?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Foldables, AR glasses, and brain-computer interfaces now rival the iPhone’s role in daily life.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: Dependence on a single device risks privacy, mental health, and digital inequality for billions.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Modular, open-source systems and decentralized apps are being built to reclaim user agency.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A future where tech supports humanity, not controls it—think wearable empathy sensors and AI co-creators.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The iPhone’s end may mark the dawn of a more integrated, ethical, and human-centered tech era.
